messages:
Aisha: Hey team — running a POC with Acme. They started getting 401s after we rotated a key this morning. Customer says they used the key from their org settings. Can we triage?
Matt: Quick question — are they sending an org header or project header?
Aisha: They sent X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp and the Authorization header with sk- key. Here’s the curl they shared:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX\" \n  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Sofia: That looks like an org/project binding mismatch. If the key is created under a project, calls must either include the correct X-Redwood-Project header or omit the org header to use project binding. If you pass an org header that doesn't match the key binding, we return 401.
Samir: FYI logs from the edge show a burst of 429s right before the 401s for that API key: 
```
edge: 2026-03-19T20:58:10Z status=429 key=sk-acme-XXXX route=/v1/generate burst_limit=120
edge: 2026-03-19T20:58:12Z status=401 key=sk-acme-XXXX reason=ORG_PROJECT_MISMATCH
```
Aisha: Interesting — customer reported intermittent 429s earlier today. Could rate limiting and a subsequent key rotation explain this?
Sofia: The two issues are separate: 429 = hit burst policy; 401 with ORG_PROJECT_MISMATCH = auth header vs key binding. But I can see a pattern where they retried with different headers which made the failure modes look linked.
Matt: For immediate unblock: 1) ask them to switch to X-Redwood-Project: acme-internal (the project the key lives in) OR 2) create an org-scoped key and rotate their app. Also have them avoid aggressive retry bursts during the POC.
Aisha: Will send that. Any quick commands to verify a key binding from our side?
Sofia: Use the admin key endpoint (support-only) to list key details: 
```
GET /v1/internal/keys/{kid}
Response: {"scope":"project","project_id":"acme-internal","created_by":"acme-admin"}
```
Matt: I pinged infra to confirm the key metadata.
deploy-bot: Token rotate event: key sk-acme-XXXX rotated by acme-admin at 2026-03-19T21:02:03Z
Samir: If they want to keep the org header, we can generate an org-scoped key and give a temporary rotation window. That avoids having to change app headers.
Jordan: On the pricing question — customer also asked if Dedicated POC capacity has any special pricing. Short answer: POC credits cover dev testing; for sustained dedicated usage we need an uplift. I'll DM to negotiate.
Aisha: Thanks Jordan. I'll update the customer with two options (switch project header OR request org key) and ask them to reduce retry aggressiveness. Also will attach the curl examples and the sample admin check.
Matt: One more note — when you send the fix, include these two lines to help them confirm success:
```
curl -I -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX\" -H \"X-Redwood-Project: acme-internal\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
# expect 200
```
Aisha: Great. I'll post the patch in the ticket and follow up later. :thumbsup:
